clue.text: She has the majority of 9-yard vehicle back, I'm glad to say

indicators.note: back tells us the vehicle word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
ha is an exclamation of satisfaction or triumph

explanation.surface: A woman owns most of a vehicle yard and is pleased to say so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TRAM into MART. The definition is cryptic: Martha's Vineyard is the US island, and VINE is most (four of six letters) of RAVINE, the answer to 9.
explanation.definitionFit: The island of Martha's Vineyard is named possessively after a Martha, so she 'has' the vine-yard.

clue.text: 26 who fell foul of 3 20 etc

definitions.meaning: Sir Thomas ..., Lord Chancellor executed in 1535 after opposing the king
etc means 'and so on', 'and others besides'

explanation.walkthrough: The 26 is THOMAS, and 3 20 is HENRY THE EIGHTH, so the first definition is a Thomas whom Henry executed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More was beheaded by Henry VIII; 'etc' stands for further unnamed items, that is, additional ones.

clue.text: Competition between right and left, about which I'm not constant

indicators.note: about which says the following phrase wraps around the word just named

parts.note: I vary: something that is not constant varies

explanation.surface: A contest between political right and left, about which the speaker keeps changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about which' puts L inside IVARY (I + VARY), giving IVALRY after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivalry is an ongoing contest or competition between two parties.

clue.text: Enrolled nurse registered in Kentish town: stature head to foot meant one had trouble with unions

indicators.note: in places the nurse and registered abbreviations inside the town's name

parts.note: Hythe is a small coastal town in Kent, south-east England
EN is the abbreviation for an enrolled nurse in Britain
R is a standard abbreviation for registered

indicators.note: head to foot says the first letter is moved down to the end of the word

parts.note: height means stature, how tall someone is

explanation.surface: A nurse registered in a Kent town, and a person's height, somehow describe a man troubled by his marriages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head to foot' moves the H of HEIGHT to the end, giving EIGHTH. 'unions' means marriages, not trade unions: Henry married six times.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's six marriages, annulments and executions of wives make him the classic man with marital trouble.

clue.text: 26 who fell foul of 3 20, or one with natural remedies

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., courtier executed in 1541 for an affair with the queen Catherine Howard
Nicholas ..., the 17th-century herbalist whose herbal of plant cures is still in print

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is THOMAS and 3 20 HENRY THE EIGHTH; 'or' links two different men sharing the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to Henry VIII's executed courtier and to the famous English herbalist who wrote on plant medicine.

clue.text: Licence for new nurse to be instructed at the start

indicators.note: new says the letters of the nurse word are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: to train is to be instructed, as an apprentice is

indicators.note: at the start takes only the opening letter of the word to

explanation.surface: Permission for a newly qualified nurse to receive instruction from day one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns NURSE into UNRES; then TRAIN, then the first letter of 'to'. Licence here is lack of restraint (as in poetic licence), not a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence in the sense of excessive freedom or lack of control is a synonym of unrestraint.

clue.text: Asian mountains: many are in couples

indicators.note: are in says the many letter sits inside the couples word

parts.note: couples are pairs
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: In the mountains of Asia, many people go about in twos.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes inside PAIRS after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pamirs are a high mountain range in Central Asia, mainly in Tajikistan.

clue.text: Patchy effect of setting foot outside dance in Paris

indicators.note: outside says the foot word goes round the dance word

parts.note: pied is French for foot, with 'in Paris' serving both pieces
bal is French for a ball or dance

explanation.surface: The look of a dancer putting a foot outside the hall at a Paris ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' serves both the foot and the dance, so both are French words; the definition is just 'Patchy', with 'effect of setting' as surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular patches of black and white, so the word describes a patchy appearance.

clue.text: People of faith get a new start from people who take over

indicators.note: get a new start says the first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: believers are people of religious faith

explanation.surface: Religious people get a fresh beginning from those who come in to replace them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get a new start' replaces the B of BELIEVERS with R.
explanation.definitionFit: Relievers are substitutes who take over a shift or duty from others, as relief workers do.

clue.text: Gorge on fruit tree with sun on it

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the vine is a fruiting plant, here loosely a tree

explanation.surface: Eat greedily from a fruit tree in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb meaning eat greedily, but it is the noun. In an across answer 'on it' puts the sun god first.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow valley, the same thing as a gorge.

clue.text: 26 who fell foul of 3 20, or one who provided protection?

definitions.meaning: Thomas ..., Henry VIII's chief minister, executed in 1540
Oliver ... ruled as Lord Protector, so he gave England a Protectorate

explanation.walkthrough: 26 is THOMAS; the second definition puns on Oliver Cromwell's title Lord Protector.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to Henry VIII's executed minister and to the later Lord Protector, playfully seen as a protector.

clue.text: Taking part in "The School for Scandal" on the football pitch?

definitions.text: Taking part in "The School for Scandal"
definitions.meaning: Joseph and Charles Surface are characters in Sheridan's play
a pitch is the ground on which a game is played

explanation.walkthrough: The School for Scandal is Sheridan's 18th-century comedy; its central brothers are named Surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A football pitch is the turf on which play takes place, and an actor could be cast as one of Sheridan's Surface brothers.

clue.text: At this point the chap is staggering, taking drug at this point only

indicators.note: taking says the drug letter is attached to what comes before

parts.note: now means at this point in time
he is the pronoun for the chap
reels means is staggering or lurching
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Right now a man is lurching about on drugs, and only here.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'At this point' gives NOW; the closing 'at this point only' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happens only at this place means it happens in no other place, the answer's sense.

clue.text: Revolutionary who set Yard to authorise action

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who set up Scotland Yard gives the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the subject of the sentence, a rebel, but it is the anagram signal for WHO SET YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To give the command that lets something proceed is to authorise action; the idiom means just tell me to.

clue.text: I leave painter among broken reeds, like the pantaloon of the sixth age

definitions.text: like the pantaloon of the sixth age

indicators.note: among says one piece is set within the other
broken says the letters of reeds are smashed and reassembled
leave tells us the letter I departs from the painter's name

parts.note: Filippo Lippi was an Italian Renaissance painter

explanation.surface: A painter departs, finding himself among smashed reeds, resembling an old buffoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns REEDS into SERED, around the trimmed painter. The definition quotes Jaques's 'seven ages' speech in As You Like It: 'the lean and slipper'd pantaloon'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's sixth age of man is the pantaloon, described as wearing slippers, so slipper-clad.

clue.text: Doing nothing gives an image to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience says we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: an idol is an image worshipped as a god

explanation.surface: Inactivity presents a picture to the onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: IDOL and IDLE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means inactive, not working, simply doing nothing.

clue.text: Whether he's a flier or a hippo?

parts.note: be he, the old subjunctive, means whether he is
a moth is a flying insect

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a creature is a flying thing or a hippopotamus.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's parts as 'be he moth': whether he is a moth. The Book of Job's behemoth is often taken to be a hippopotamus.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth, the huge beast of Job, is traditionally identified with the hippopotamus.

clue.text: Fourth article may be Russian

parts.note: IV is the Roman numeral four, as in a regnal number
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fourth item in a list could be Russian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth' hints at Ivan IV, Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is the typical Russian man's name, so stands for a Russian by example.

clue.text: 26 who fell foul of 3 second call during elevated meal

indicators.note: during says the call word comes in the middle of the meal word
elevated in a down answer means the meal word is written upwards

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
a beck is a call or summoning gesture, as in beck and call

explanation.surface: A summons comes in the middle of a high tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' gives AET in this down answer. '3 second' is Henry the Second, not the Eighth: Thomas Becket was killed in 1170 after quarrelling with Henry II.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury, fell out with Henry II and was murdered in his cathedral.

clue.text: Homes for team during screenplay

indicators.note: during says the team goes inside the other piece
play means the letters of screen are loosened and moved about

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A team's accommodation while they shoot a film script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screenplay' must be split: its second half is the anagram signal working on its first half, giving RENCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Residences are dwellings, the places where people make their homes.

clue.text: White robe is partly coloured on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the coloured word wraps around the little word is
partly says only part of the coloured word is used

parts.note: chromatic means coloured

explanation.surface: A white garment has some colour around its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' trims the colour word to CHROM. A chrisom is the white robe put on a baby at baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom is the white christening robe once given to an infant at baptism.

clue.text: See 3
Kindest characters go wrong in quarry, possibility for next year?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters and the error word inside the quarry word

parts.note: prey is the quarry a hunter pursues

indicators.note: characters means the letters of kindest are taken as loose type to be reset

parts.note: to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: Kind people's personalities go astray in a stone pit, perhaps next year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' turns KINDEST into SIDENTK. The puzzle appeared in 2004, when John Kerry was challenging George W Bush for the US presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2004 a Kerry presidency was a possible outcome of the coming November election, hence next year.

clue.text: They have it in the passage

definitions.text: They have it in the passage

parts.words: They have it in the passage
parts.note: the Speaker's call when a vote passes is that those voting yes have it, and the passage is of a bill

explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' looks like a corridor, but it is the passing of legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour carry a parliamentary bill to its passage, as in the Speaker's formula.

clue.text: Debauchee to attend around monarch, returning at length

indicators.note: returning says the assembled piece is read backwards
around says the listening word goes round the monarch letter

parts.note: to hear is to attend, to listen
K is the abbreviation for king
an ell is an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A rake goes to listen around the king, coming back at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts K inside HEAR to give HEKAR, which 'returning' turns into RAKEH.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakehell is a dissolute libertine, a debauched man.

clue.text: 26 who fell foul of 3 20 to base consent on returns

indicators.note: on returns says each of the two words is turned back on itself

parts.note: low means base, mean
yes signals consent

explanation.surface: A cardinal disgraced by the king builds agreement on rebounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on returns' turns LOW and YES each in place, giving WOL and SEY. Cardinal Thomas Wolsey lost Henry VIII's favour over the divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Thomas Wolsey fell from Henry VIII's favour and died in 1530 facing treason charges.

clue.text: Wife has husbands, alternative personalities?

indicators.note: has links the wife to the men who follow

parts.note: Dutch is cockney slang for wife, from 'duchess of Fife'
husbands are men, as in 'man and wife'

explanation.surface: A woman has multiple husbands: perhaps she has split personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'or I'm a Dutchman', in which a Dutchman is the alternative person one would rather be if a claim is false.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'if that's true I'm a Dutchman', a Dutchman is the alternative self the speaker would become.

clue.text: Zero in mathematics complicated? I'm not sure

indicators.note: in places the zero letter inside the rearranged subject
complicated says the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: maths is the British short form of mathematics
O looks like a zero

explanation.surface: Unsure of themselves after scoring nothing in a difficult maths test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges MATHS to THMAS, with O inside. A doubting Thomas, after the apostle, is a sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubting Thomas, named after the apostle who doubted, is a person who says they are unsure.
